questions.q: A boutique wants crisp, punchy track spotlights on its garments, using a filament source. Choose:
questions.n: Halogen gives a whiter, more directional beam.

questions.q: For the warehouse section of a large furniture showroom, the suitable light source is:
questions.n: Good efficacy and acceptable color rendering.

questions.q: Brightness (luminance) of a glare source is expressed in:
questions.n: Footcandles measure illuminance; footlamberts measure luminance.

questions.q: Heating a tungsten wire until it glows gives perfect color rendering (CRI 100) but wastes about 90% of the energy as heat. This is the:
questions.n: That inefficiency is why codes restrict them.

questions.q: For a gym or car showroom with a high ceiling, the classic HID source with crisp white light is:
questions.n: Metal halide adds halide salts to the arc for good color rendering.

questions.q: A room with both computer screens and paper work surfaces should get:
o: Indirect ambient light plus a task light at each desk
questions.n: Indirect light cuts screen glare; task lights serve paper work.

questions.q: Which source is mercury-free, starts instantly, and is the practical baseline for meeting lighting power density limits?
questions.n: Fluorescent and HID lamps contain mercury.

questions.q: A restaurant wants warm-dimming decorative lamps with a CRI of 100 to flatter the food. Choose:
questions.n: Filament lamps glow warmer as they dim.

questions.q: A 24/7 underground car park needs instant-on, dimmable lighting tied to emergency backup. The modern standard is:
questions.n: Instant start, dimmable, and low LPD.

questions.q: A comfortable general task-lighting level is about:
questions.n: Offices are typically 300–500 lux.

questions.q: The classic municipal street light, warm amber and efficient, is:
questions.n: HPS dominated roadway lighting before LEDs.

questions.q: Illuminance, the light actually landing on a surface, is measured in:
questions.n: Lux = lumens per square meter.

questions.q: A complete lighting unit, with lamp, housing, optics and ballast or driver, is a:
questions.n: The lamp is just the light source.

questions.q: A warehouse's high-bay lights go dark for 10–15 minutes after every brief power dip. That's the restrike delay typical of:
o: HID lamps such as metal halide and HPS
questions.n: Hot arc tubes must cool before they reignite.

questions.q: Today's default source for efficient general lighting in every building type is:
questions.n: LEDs lead in efficacy and life.

questions.q: Uniform office lighting from louvered troffers was traditionally done with:
questions.n: Linear fluorescents were the office standard.

questions.q: Traditionally, a long vehicular tunnel where drivers only need contrast could be lit with the monochromatic yellow:
questions.n: LPS is very efficient but renders no color.

questions.q: Which family runs on an ionized gas arc, needs a ballast, and must cool before restriking?
questions.n: HID lamps take minutes to restrike after a power dip.

questions.q: Which lighting must NOT be on occupancy sensors?
questions.n: Egress lighting has to stay available.

questions.q: To bring out the texture of a rough plaster wall, use:
o: Recessed lights close to the wall, grazing it
questions.n: Grazing light exaggerates texture.

questions.q: Custom-bent glass tubes of excited noble gas for script signs are:
questions.n: Neon uses high-voltage transformers and cold cathodes.

questions.q: A coastal highway needs light that cuts through fog and rain, and color rendering doesn't matter. Specify:
questions.n: Warm, long-wavelength light scatters less in fog.

questions.q: A halogen lamp burns hotter and brighter than a plain incandescent because:
o: Halogen gas redeposits evaporated tungsten back on the filament
questions.n: The halogen cycle allows a hotter filament in a quartz envelope.

questions.q: Bathroom vanity sconces belong:
o: On both sides of the mirror
questions.n: Side lighting lights the face evenly without shadows.

questions.q: A UV arc inside a tube excites a phosphor coating to make visible light in a:
questions.n: The phosphor converts UV into white light.

questions.q: Under-cabinet task lighting is usually a:
questions.n: Low-profile strips fit under cabinets.
